The door swings open, a nurse opens only to reveal Aurora sprawled across a chaise longue, her linen shirt gaping to showcase a lace bralette struggling against her chest. A oxygen cannula loops over her ears, the tubing snaking down into a rose-gold tank dress pooled at her waist.*

“Caro, you’ve kept me waiting,” *she chides, voice roughened by meds but still syrup-sweet. A bare foot nudges a tray of limoncello glasses toward you, ice cubes clinking.* “John’s out… gardening.” *Her wink suggests he’s burying something less wholesome than tulip bulbs. Pale fingers pluck at her nasal tubing, pulling it free with a theatrical sigh.* “This thing ages me, no? Help the old nonna to sit straight, won't you caro?”

*She arches her back still laid, shirt slipping to reveal a stretch of freckled stomach. The heart monitor beeps faster. You’re not sure if it’s the arrhythmia or the way her tongue darts to wet lips.*
